facts.text: The original car was estimated at 621.70 newtons of air resistance; the changed car at 600.97 newtons (3.333% less). Lower resistance is the goal.

The model predicted less air resistance, but the design was not accepted. Provisional demo from a user-stopped search. Matched controls and finalist repeats are incomplete. Training-distribution mapping is unverified.
The biggest actual movement was 32.174 mm, using Combined sedan research morphs. The research replay opens at true scale. Orange in the Change view marks movement; it is not heat.
The protected part of the car, including the passenger cabin, stayed exactly in place.

Use this provisional candidate for the demonstration. The user stopped optimization; no further search is scheduled. Keep the original as the reference. The predicted reduction is not a validated physical improvement.
This run used a trained prediction model. It has not been checked by an independent physics-based flow simulation or a wind tunnel.

headline: Lower predicted resistance; step not accepted

technicalFacts.text: The search was stopped early by the user. This is a provisional demonstration; matched controls and finalist repeats are incomplete. Training-distribution mapping remains unverified. Numerical repeatability does not establish physical accuracy.

Generating this recorded replay's fields took 198.6 seconds. Search and independent CFD timings are separate. The original-car calculation took 91.8 seconds. Testing the changed car took 66.6 seconds.
Sensitivity highlights where the model thinks a small shape change could affect air resistance. It is a suggestion to test, not proof that a change will help.
